model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance or loss curves of several language model variants over a range of steps or iterations, with the x-axis representing the number of steps on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^5, marked with tick labels at 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, and 100000. The y-axis, labeled "Perplexity," is on a linear scale ranging from approximately 0 to 100, with tick marks at intervals of 20. Five distinct lines are shown: a blue solid line for "StrmLLM (n=64)" which starts at a high perplexity value (around 90) and decreases steeply before leveling off near 20; an orange solid line for "SepLLM (n=64)" starting slightly lower than the blue line and converging to a similar final value; a green solid line for "SepLLM (n=64, H)" that follows a similar trend but remains slightly below the orange line; a red solid line for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" which is consistently lower than the green line, starting around 70 and ending near 15; and a dark blue solid line for "SepLLM (n=128)" which is the lowest of all, starting near 70 and stabilizing around 10. All lines exhibit a steep initial decline followed by a gradual flattening, indicating convergence, with the dark blue line showing the best performance (lowest perplexity) across the entire range.
